subject: Renewal: FreshCart — scale safeguard & benchmark request

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal check-in + competitor benchmark ping

Hi Lauren —

Quick note as we start Q3 planning: our renewal with Redwood is up in late September. We’re running a side-by-side test with another vendor (PerfScale) and the ops team flagged two areas where they think they can shave cost at our scale: longer token caching and a slightly different quantized runtime.

Before the execs go farther down that route, we wanted to understand whether Redwood can offer any short-term mitigations that avoid a full migration:
- a temporary capacity uplift for September peak (20% headroom)
- a targeted throughput benchmark against our Production workload (20M tokens/day window)
- a proposal for a 12–18 month renewal term that keeps unit price flat if we commit to a capacity band

Can your team run a focused benchmark and share a short mitigation proposal? Marcus (ops) is around for logistics — cc’d.

Thanks,
Alisha
Sr. Procurement Manager | FreshCart

Marissa / Ben — forwarding FreshCart ask. Summary: they’re in a side-by-side with PerfScale and want a benchmark + short-term capacity uplift and a renewal term that stabilizes pricing. FreshCart is mid-market but high-volume in the grocery vertical; they matter for our East/West presence and are vocal at the platform level.

Proposed play:
1) run a 72-hour production-slice benchmark using their prod prompts (Marcus will share) and produce: latency distribution, per-token cost delta, cache hit % for prefixes
2) offer a September peak uplift (non-recurring, month credit model) + an optional committed-usage band for 12 months with a modest discount tied to baseline commit
3) include an ops runbook for prefix caching and a QA window to reduce false positives in perf comparisons

Can you two carve out a DR plan and draft the benchmark matrix? I’ll own the commercial note. Need a draft we can send to Alisha by next Tue (7/6) to keep momentum.

—Lauren

Hi Alisha / Marcus —

Thanks for the heads-up. We can absolutely run a focused benchmark and a temporary uplift plan. High-level commitment from Redwood:
- 72-hour Production-slice benchmark (we’ll use a 24/7 rolling window you identify; include a control traffic shard)
- For September peak: a one-month 20% capacity buffer available as a reserved pool (no infra change required) + an option to convert to a 3-month reserved at a modest discount if you like the safeguard
- Renewal term options: 12 months (flat unit price with elasticity band) or 18 months (2% unit discount + guaranteed latency SLOs for the committed band)

Action items we need from your side:
- Marcus: please share a 72-hour sample token dump and the prompt set you want benchmarked (we’ll handle anonymization)
- Procurement: confirm whether FreshCart prefers a credit model for the one-month uplift vs. a billable reserved pool

We’ll produce a short results deck + a one-page proposal. Expect our draft by Tue 7/6.

Best,
Lauren

Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: FreshCart benchmark results + scale safeguard proposal

Team — final deliverable ready to share with FreshCart. I’ve attached two files: the benchmark matrix (freshcart-benchmark-matrix.xlsx) and the commercial proposal (redwood-scale-safeguard-proposal.pdf). Highlights below for the executive summary we’ll push to Alisha:

Executive summary:
- Performance: in the 72-hour production slice we matched PerfScale median latency and beat them on 95th percentile by ~8% once prefix cache warmed (see Sheet 2 for percentiles)
- Cost: per-token cost is within 6% of PerfScale on baseline config; with a targeted cache and batching tune we can achieve parity or slightly better on their workload
- Ops: recommend a one-month 20% reserved capacity buffer provided as prepaid credit (applies to September billing period). This avoids provisioning delays and is procurement-friendly.
- Renewal options: 12 mo = flat unit price + commit band; 18 mo = 2% unit discount + extended support window (SLA addendum).

Next steps:
1) Lauren + Ben to send a one-page MAM (mutual action plan) + the two attachments to Alisha today
2) Schedule 30-min executive readout w/ FreshCart and our Solutions lead for 7/21 (they requested 7/20 but we’ve got limited exec availability; 7/21 still works for their team)

Thanks — draft MAM below for copy/paste: 
- Week of 7/14: share benchmark deck + proposal (today)
- Week of 7/14: FreshCart execs review
- 7/21: executive readout + alignment on renewal term
- Sept: apply 20% uplift credit during peak week (customer to nominate peak window)

—Marissa
